llm:
Phillips 66 reported third-quarter earnings of $402 million. Special items produced an after-tax loss of $1.0 billion, largely from an impairment of the Alliance Refinery. Excluding those items, adjusted earnings were $1.4 billion, or $3.18 per share—an increase of $1.1 billion from the second quarter, reflecting a substantial improvement in Refining and continued strong contributions from Midstream, Chemicals, and Marketing and Specialties. The adjusted effective income tax rate was 16%.

Operating cash flow was $2.2 billion, including a $776 million working-capital benefit and $905 million of cash distributions from equity affiliates. Excluding the working-capital benefit, cash from operations was $1.4 billion. Capital spending totaled $552 million, of which $311 million went to growth projects, including a $150 million investment in NOVONIX. The company paid $394 million in dividends and made $500 million of early debt repayment during the quarter. Cash increased from $2.2 billion at the start of the quarter to $2.9 billion at the end. Phillips 66 said it had reduced debt by $1 billion so far this year and returned approximately $29 billion to shareholders since its formation. In October, it raised the quarterly dividend to $0.92 per share.

Midstream adjusted pre-tax income was $642 million, up $326 million from the prior quarter. Transportation contributed $254 million, up $30 million. NGL and Other contributed $357 million, compared with $83 million in the second quarter; the increase was primarily due to a $224 million unrealized investment gain related to NOVONIX and inventory impacts. Phillips 66 acquired a 16% interest in NOVONIX in September. The Sweeny fractionation complex averaged a record 383,000 barrels per day, while the Freeport LPG export facility loaded 41 cargoes. DCP Midstream’s adjusted pre-tax income rose $22 million to $31 million, mainly on improved margins and hedging impacts. Construction at the Sweeny Hub was approximately one-third complete, with about 70% of its capital already spent, and construction of Phillips 66 Partners’ C2G pipeline was completed.

Chemicals delivered adjusted pre-tax income of $634 million, down $23 million from the second quarter. Olefins & Polyolefins achieved record adjusted pre-tax income of $613 million, up $20 million, supported by higher polyethylene sales volumes and strong demand, partly offset by higher utility costs; global O&P utilization was 102%. Adjusted pre-tax income for SA&S fell $45 million as margins began to normalize after tight market conditions. Phillips 66 received $632 million in cash distributions from CPChem during the quarter.

Refining’s adjusted pre-tax income improved by $890 million to $184 million, driven by higher realized margins across all regions. Realized margins rose 119% to $8.57 per barrel, with market capture increasing to 44% from 22% in the prior quarter. The 3:2:1 market crack was $19.44 per barrel, compared with $17.76. Higher market crack spreads, lower RIN costs, and improved product differentials supported results; the distillate and gasoline cracks increased by $1.55 and $1.92 per barrel, respectively. Secondary-product losses improved by $0.40 to $1.98 per barrel as NGL prices strengthened, while the feedstock advantage declined by $0.26 to $0.01 per barrel. The Other category reduced realized margins by $5.01 per barrel. Pre-tax turnaround costs declined to $81 million from $118 million. Crude utilization was 86%, versus 88% in the second quarter, reflecting downtime at the Alliance Refinery, which was safely shut down on August 28 ahead of Hurricane Ida. Clean product yield was 84%, up 2% from the prior quarter, supported by improved FCC operations.

Marketing & Other adjusted pre-tax income was $547 million, compared with $479 million in the second quarter; Marketing & Other increased by $62 million. Refined-product exports averaged 209,000 barrels per day. Specialties adjusted pre-tax income rose to $93 million from $87 million, largely on improved oil margins. Phillips 66 is converting 600 branded retail sites in California to sell renewable diesel produced at the Rodeo facility, which is expected to have more than 50,000 barrels per day of renewable-fuel production capacity upon completion. Corporate and Other adjusted pre-tax costs were $230 million, an improvement of $40 million from the prior quarter.

The company announced an agreement to acquire all publicly held units of Phillips 66 Partners in an all-equity transaction, which it said would simplify its corporate structure and position it to create greater value for both companies’ investors. It also announced greenhouse-gas targets to reduce the carbon-emissions intensity of its operations by 2030. For the fourth quarter, Phillips 66 expects pre-tax turnaround expenses of $110 million to $140 million and pre-tax Corporate and Other costs of $240 million to $250 million.
